metadata.description: Retrieval evaluation dataset for PubMed hypertension articles. 10 open-access PMC review articles spanning management guidelines, pharmacotherapy, lifestyle/adherence, and comorbidities.

questions.question: What blood pressure reduction do standardized treatment protocols achieve compared to usual care?
questions.answer: Reductions in systolic and diastolic BP with STPs compared to usual care were 6.7 (95% CI 3.7-9.8) mmHg and 2.6 (1.2-4.1) mmHg, respectively (p < 0.001 for both). BP control achieved was 57% in the STP group compared to 24% in the usual care group.

questions.question: Are standardized hypertension treatment protocols safe? What about side effects?
questions.answer: The overall incidence of any adverse events was 14.5% versus 13.5% (RR 1.27 [0.88-1.82]) with STPs and usual care, respectively, showing no statistically significant difference in safety.

questions.question: What is the recommended initial blood pressure reduction target for a hypertensive emergency?
questions.answer: BP >= 180/120 mmHg with end-organ damage has been defined as an emergency, requiring a reduction of BP by 20-25% within the first hour, followed by a gradual decrease.

questions.question: What blood pressure target is recommended for ischemic stroke patients?
questions.answer: Ischemic stroke was the most commonly discussed end-organ damage type (n = 8 guidelines), with a target BP range of 130-180/90-105 mmHg.

questions.question: When should treatment be started for patients with both hypertension and diabetes according to the Saudi guidelines?
questions.answer: In people with hypertension and diabetes, it is recommended to initiate therapy when BP is equal to or higher than 130/80 mmHg and target a BP level below 130/80 mmHg.

questions.question: What role does renal denervation play in treating resistant hypertension?
questions.answer: Ultrasound and radiofrequency renal denervation showed remarkable BP lowering in off-medicated uncontrolled hypertension patients by 6.3 and 5 mmHg, respectively. In late 2023, the US FDA approved both radiofrequency- and ultrasound-based renal denervation devices.

questions.question: Should SGLT2 inhibitors be used in CKD patients who don't have diabetes?
questions.answer: SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for CKD patients with or without diabetes if eGFR is at least 20 ml/min/1.73 m2 to reduce cardiac and renal outcomes.

questions.question: How effective is tirzepatide at lowering blood pressure?
questions.answer: Tirzepatide led to the largest decreases in SBP (-6.45 mmHg) and DBP (-3.64 mmHg) among GLP-1-based agents studied.

questions.question: What percentage of patients with resistant hypertension are overweight or obese?
questions.answer: Obesity ranks among the most significant modifiable risk factors for resistant hypertension, with 56-91% of patients with resistant hypertension classified as overweight or obese.

questions.question: Does semaglutide reduce cardiovascular risk in addition to lowering blood pressure?
questions.answer: The SELECT Trial showed semaglutide resulted in a 20% reduction in the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke.

questions.question: What happens to people who don't take their blood pressure medicine regularly?
questions.answer: Poor adherence to antihypertensive treatment significantly increased all-cause mortality (HR: 1.32 [1.14, 1.51], p < 0.001) and was linked to elevated cardiovascular mortality (HR: 1.61 [1.43, 1.78], p < 0.001).

questions.question: Does the mortality risk from medication non-adherence differ between new and long-term hypertension patients?
questions.answer: Newly treated patients had a lower hazard ratio (HR: 1.22 [1.07, 1.37]) compared to those who had been on antihypertensive medication for a longer time (HR: 1.75 [1.33, 2.18]) (p = 0.02).

questions.question: How much salt should someone with high blood pressure eat per day?
questions.answer: The ISH recommends intake of less than 2 g sodium (approximately 5 g salt or one teaspoon) per day.

questions.question: How much can exercise lower blood pressure in people with hypertension?
questions.answer: Aerobic and dynamic resistance training interventions reduce office and daytime ambulatory BP, with greater reductions occurring in those with established hypertension (up to 8.3/5.2 mmHg office BP reductions). A one-metabolic equivalent increment (MET) in cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with 8% hypertension risk reduction.

questions.question: What are the main reasons patients don't take their blood pressure medication?
questions.answer: A meta-integration of 27 qualitative studies identified five barrier themes: lack of medication literacy, difficulty adapting to roles, reduced sense of benefit from treatment, limited access to healthcare resources, and unintentional nonadherence (primarily forgetfulness). A meta-analysis of 27 million patients showed nonadherence was common worldwide (27%-40%) between 2010 and 2020.

questions.question: What percentage of people with diabetes also have hypertension?
questions.answer: About 70% of diabetic patients suffer from hypertension, which is roughly twice as frequent in people with diabetes as it is in people without it.

questions.question: How much does lowering blood pressure reduce complications in patients with type 2 diabetes?
questions.answer: The UKPDS found that by lowering BP, the combined risk of microvascular and macrovascular complications from type 2 diabetes was lowered by 24%.

questions.question: How common is resistant hypertension in patients with chronic kidney disease?
questions.answer: Up to half of patients with CKD meet apparent treatment-resistant hypertension criteria using the 2017 ACC/AHA target BP less than 130/80 mmHg. These patients are at 30-40% higher risk of cardiovascular and kidney outcomes compared to nonresistant hypertension.

questions.question: How much does reducing dietary sodium help with resistant hypertension in CKD?
questions.answer: Intake of AHA and KDIGO recommended dietary sodium (less than 2.4 g/day) leads to an average of 10/4 mmHg drop in BP, even in patients with resistant hypertension associated with CKD.

questions.question: What is the global burden of uncontrolled hypertension?
questions.answer: According to the World Health Organization, there are 1.4 billion people with hypertension worldwide, of whom only 14% have their blood pressure under control.

questions.question: What blood pressure targets do VA CPG guidelines recommend for patients with diabetes, and does recent peer-reviewed literature support those targets?
questions.answer: The VA/DoD CPG recommends treating to a systolic BP goal of less than 140 mmHg for patients over 60 with type 2 diabetes, with added benefit below 130 mmHg. The Saudi Heart Association 2023 guidelines (PMC10069676) independently recommend initiating therapy at 130/80 mmHg and targeting below 130/80 mmHg for hypertensive patients with diabetes, supporting an aggressive approach. Cross-source evidence converges on 130/80 mmHg as the target for diabetic patients.
questions.notes: Tests whether agent discovers both VA CPG and pubmed-hypertension articles for a diabetes+hypertension question

questions.question: What does the evidence say about why patients don't take their blood pressure medications, and what do VA guidelines recommend to address this?
questions.answer: PubMed research (PMC10976505) identifies five barrier themes: lack of medication literacy, difficulty adapting to roles, reduced sense of benefit, limited healthcare access, and unintentional nonadherence (27-40% of patients worldwide). VA CPG guidelines recommend patient education, simplified regimens, and follow-up monitoring to improve adherence. The mortality impact is significant: poor adherence increases all-cause mortality by 32% and cardiovascular mortality by 61% (PMC11874117).
questions.notes: Tests cross-dataset reasoning: barriers from pubmed literature + recommendations from VA CPG + mortality data

questions.question: For a patient with resistant hypertension and chronic kidney disease, what are the treatment options including newer therapies?
questions.answer: VA CPG guidelines recommend stepped-care pharmacotherapy including diuretics, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, and calcium channel blockers. Beyond standard care, recent evidence shows renal denervation (FDA-approved late 2023) can lower BP by 5-6.3 mmHg (PMC11152838), dietary sodium restriction below 2.4 g/day achieves 10/4 mmHg reduction in CKD patients (PMC11296285), and GLP-1 receptor agonists may help patients with comorbid obesity (PMC11377134). Up to 50% of CKD patients meet treatment-resistant criteria.
questions.notes: Tests multi-article reasoning within pubmed-hypertension plus VA CPG guidelines

questions.question: What lifestyle changes can help lower blood pressure, and how much can they help?
questions.answer: The ISH position paper (PMC10713007) quantifies lifestyle interventions: sodium intake below 2g/day, aerobic exercise achieving up to 8.3/5.2 mmHg reductions in established hypertension, and each 1-MET increase in fitness associated with 8% risk reduction. VA CPG guidelines recommend lifestyle modifications as part of initial treatment. Standardized treatment protocols incorporating both pharmacological and non-pharmacological approaches achieved 57% BP control vs 24% with usual care (PMC11773677).
questions.notes: Tests lifestyle management across VA CPG + ISH position paper + STP evidence

questions.question: What are the latest treatment advances for hypertension that go beyond the current VA CPG recommendations?
questions.answer: Several advances go beyond current VA CPG guidelines: renal denervation using ultrasound and radiofrequency (FDA-approved 2023, 5-6.3 mmHg reductions), GLP-1 receptor agonists for resistant hypertension in obese patients (semaglutide showed 20% MACE reduction in SELECT trial), SGLT2 inhibitors for CKD patients regardless of diabetes status (if eGFR >= 20), and standardized treatment protocols achieving dramatically better BP control (57% vs 24%). These findings from 2023-2025 literature suggest potential updates to VA CPG treatment algorithms.
questions.notes: Key cross-dataset test: agent should identify what pubmed literature adds beyond VA CPG and note the temporal difference
